summary:
Raconteur examines how conversational AI is reshaping European rail ticket distribution. Eurostar has integrated live journey and fare search into ChatGPT, though bookings still complete on Eurostar.com. Traffic from AI platforms to Eurostar's site grew fivefold between January 2025 and June 2026, but AI drove under 1% of total bookings between May and July, so volumes stay small. Chief commercial officer Francois Le Doze says search habits are shifting as travellers use conversational tools to plan journeys. SNCF Connect, Trainline and Omio are building similar tools, reflecting a shift in the competitive battle from who sells the ticket to where passengers begin searching.

The piece frames this as a fight for the passenger interface. Third-party platforms deliver new customers, particularly on international routes, but when discovery moves off operator channels, operators lose control over which routes, fares and brands appear first. Pushing transactions into AI tools raises unresolved questions about payments, liability and accountability when trips go wrong.

Regulatory context: the European Commission wants to simplify multi-operator ticketing, open rail inventory access and curb self-preferencing by dominant platforms. The Community of European Railway and Infrastructure Companies opposes mandatory distribution rules and fixed commissions, with executive director Alberto Mazzola warning such mandates could entrench platform gatekeepers. The risk is swapping traditional gatekeepers for tech platforms.

The UK is going the other way, building a central national storefront. Great British Railways will replace the websites and apps of 14 Department for Transport operators with one platform while independent retailers like Trainline still compete. Transport secretary Heidi Alexander promises one railway, one brand, one organisation in charge. Great Western Railway is preparing for public ownership while building customer data and loyalty systems; HS2 will expose integration challenges around connections, unified disruption alerts and accountability. A single interface cannot fix fractured fares, separate customer records or split liability beneath it.

AI generated a very small share of Eurostar's total bookings
Travellers increasingly use conversational tools to plan journeys as search habits change quickly

claims.claim: Great British Railways will replace websites and apps across Department for Transport operators with a single platform

Eurostar's ChatGPT integration redirects passengers to Eurostar.com to complete payment, as does SNCF Connect on its own site
